도쿄 라멘 명소 Ramen Jazzy Beats입니다. 

추천받은 특상 쇼유 라멘을 주문했는데요, 국물은 토종닭과 4종류의 말린 생선으로 감칠맛을 더한 진한 간장 스프가 특징이에요. 스트레이트 면이 국물을 잘 머금고, 저온 조리된 돼지 차슈, 튀긴 우엉, 교토산 파, 완벽한 반숙 계란이 토핑으로 올라가 있답니다.

특히 차슈는 간장과 소금으로 각각 양념되어 부드럽고 깊은 맛을 자랑했어요. 김을 국물에 풀면 해산물 풍미가 한층 더해지며, 재료 하나하나에서 정성을 느낄 수 있는 한 그릇이었답니다.

도쿄에서만 맛볼 수 있는 특별한 라멘으로 추천드려요! 

 [Ramen Jazzy Beats] @ramen_jazzybeats
- 위치: Tokyo, Meguro City, Kamimeguro, 3−5−25 나카메구로 철도 고가 아래
- 영업: 월.화 휴무, 11:30 - 14:30, 17:30 - 22:00
- 가격: 특상 쇼유 라멘 (1,780엔)

Let me introduce Ramen Jazzy Beats, a must-visit ramen spot in Tokyo for true ramen enthusiasts.

I tried their signature Special Shoyu Ramen, and it was truly impressive. The broth, made with premium free-range chicken and four types of dried fish, had a rich soy sauce flavor. The straight noodles perfectly absorbed the broth, and the toppings included sous vide pork chashu, crispy burdock root, Kyoto-grown green onions, and a perfectly soft-boiled egg.

The chashu stood out with its delicate seasoning—one with soy sauce and the other with salt—melting in your mouth like a fine dish. Adding seaweed to the broth elevated the umami, making the flavors even richer.

Every element of this bowl reflected incredible care and attention to detail. A unique ramen experience you can only find in Tokyo—highly recommended!

[Ramen Jazzy Beats] @ramen_jazzybeats
• Location: Tokyo, Meguro City, Kamimeguro, 3−5−25, under the Naka-Meguro train tracks
• Hours: Closed Mondays and Tuesdays, 11:30 AM – 2:30 PM, 5:30 PM – 10:00 PM
• Price: Special Shoyu Ramen (¥1,780)

Dedicated shopping day in Osaka 💴".
transcription: Come with us for a dedicated shopping day in Osaka, Japan. First we took the subway over to Namba, which is a huge shopping district where we found a super book off, which is basically a value village that also has a big upscale section. Pricing was okay, there were a couple of steels, but you really had to look for them. After that we hit a big conveyor belt sushi place that filled it into on his last trip after crushing the aquariums where the fish we walked down to Senchin Mai, which is a huge bizarre dedicated solely to kitchenware. Literally every cooking utensil machine gadget and tool under the sun was for sale on this street. And Phil found himself a nice stainless steel petty knife for a pretty good deal after shopping around a few different stores. Then we got some coffees and a little snack before heading to Hanoia to try and find some heavy denim, but they were sold out of our sizes. So we just kind of aimlessly wandered around for the rest of the afternoon. Super easy to stumble and vintage stores, find a couple good deals, and then finally we ended the day with some fresh made Okonomiyaki and Takayaki. Stay tuned for for more Japan content.

Tokyo Overlooked - Livehouses 🎵

Local livehouses often get overlooked by bigger and more popular nightlife activities like clubbing in Tokyo.  While clubbing can be fun, going to a local livehouse in Tokyo is such a unique and authentic experience, it can create amazing meaningful memories. 

🏠Livehouses - 
They usually refer to small Japanese live music venues that often double as bars.  But here, you can meet friendly locals who want to get to know you.  This was my first time ever going to a livehouse in Tokyo, and I can safely say that I will be going to another livehouse show on my next night out.
